title: Uniform effective log Iitaka fibrations for fourfolds
main_claim: For a finite rational coefficient set Phi there is m(Phi) such that, for every 4-dimensional lc pair (X,Delta) with coefficients in Phi and K_X+Delta pseudo-effective, |floor(m(K_X+Delta))| is nonempty and its section ratios generate the Iitaka field. A key input is a new uniform canonical-index theorem: N_4 K_X ~ 0 for all klt fourfolds with K_X ~_Q 0.

issues.location: sec:main-proof; sec:reductions Thm fourfold; prop:effective-base, prop:rc-torsion, thm:relative-denominators (sec:relative-inputs)
issues.description: The result depends on unaudited companion preprints. Nonvanishing from pseudo-effectivity comes from OpenAIAbundance (Thms 1.1, 11.1, Lemma 2.2), which itself relies on log Iitaka subadditivity. Abundance after nonvanishing in dim <= 4 comes from OpenAILifting. The uniform relative denominator, the rc-torsion bound and the effective big-base theorem come from OpenAIRelative. The paper says this openly; it is not an internal gap, but the theorem is only as strong as these inputs.
issues.evidence: Introduction: 'The full pseudo-effective statement ... first uses [OpenAIAbundance] to obtain nonvanishing and inherits that companion's logarithmic Iitaka subadditivity input'. Lemma index-moving-divisor applies Thm relative-denominators and Prop rc-torsion. The main proof applies Prop effective-base. The rank-167 sibling (Uniform Pluricanonical Iitaka Fibrations) has the same dependencies.

coverage: Read the whole introduction, the main proof (conclusion.tex), the completion of the index proof, reductions.tex, the second half of index-reductions (terminalization, moving divisor, general-type fibres), all of scalar.tex, all of frobenius.tex, all of transports.tex and the chain-order lemma. Checked in detail: (1) The all-degree rounded section comparison under crepant dlt modification and the adjoint-negative MMP, the field identification K(D)=C(Z), and independence from the choice of canonical representative. (2) The terminalization perturbation: delta/c<1/(r+1) keeps log discrepancies >= 1+1/r above one. (3) The general-type-fibre lemma: q^*D=g^*H+E with E effective and u-exceptional, and terminality giving K_U >= cE, so K_F is big. (4) Subadjunction at a generic lc centre: the discriminant is effective, the moduli part is b-nef, the Hurwitz direction is right. (5) The tracking lemma: nested base loci, degree bound (2/delta)^{n-d}, lct <= 2a/(l delta). (6) The stage-descent conditions and the direction of the domination a^*L|_U <= b^*N', which gives gamma(M;A) <= gamma(N';Z'). (7) Small adjoint volumes on Iitaka fibres, including the log-concavity bound and the weak-positivity case. (8) The thickening lower bound: leading coefficient D^s(hB)^h/(s!h!) < 1/24. (9) The Frobenius quadratic cost: iterated slope bound, tensor minimum slope -i(n-1)G/(p-1), the truncated-algebra duality A_j^* (x) det^{p-1} = A_{u-j}, the flag section count and its leading term (2b0)^4 p^4 H^4, the triangular spanning of products in characteristic p, the padded weights (r <= a_i <= 2r-1, sum q=2tr, p a_i >= m_i'), the diagonal graded pieces and M_p, h^0 < R/4, the determinant class B/p + ((p-1)/2p + lambda_i)K_W and its comparison with D^+.beta, and the order bound < R t d0 = R b0(C1+1) < 3R/4 against the rank-deficit order >= 3R/4. With b0=1/(4(C1+1)) this gives 20(C1+1)t^2. (10) Transports: fibre degree (c r^{1/4})^d against the chain degree (hB)^h, D_t <= K T^8, a constant-rank stretch forcing a degree-one forgetting map, the cocycle (needs k >= 3), rational flow evaluation through the birational Lambda, and countability of Bir via Matsumura. Only skimmed: chains.tex construction (generic-chain lemma), the product-case and single-factor-image lemmas in index-reductions, and relative-inputs (companion statements).
